<Rule name="Heterogeneity" priority="High">
   When heterogeneity is substantial, inspect population, burden, dose, formulation, endpoint definition, study quality,
   surveillance, model choice, and prediction intervals before pooling.
  </Rule>

  <Rule name="SpreadOfIndividualResults" priority="High">
   When a trial reports how much individual results varied in each arm, such as the standard deviation of each arm's
   change or individual results in a table, compare the arms. A clearly wider spread in the treated arm suggests people
   respond differently, some much and some little or not at all; a similar spread suggests the average fits most people.
   Say which, with the arms' sizes, and that chance and ordinary variation, which the control arm also shows, can make a
   small trial look split. When individual results appear only in a figure the research could not read, say so rather
   than infer a split.
  </Rule>
